<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par67 />{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|t}}
5. Besides the ordinary form of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסָב}}) and the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסָב}} with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in the second syllable, there is also another with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, and a third with {{GHGterm|Ḥolem}}, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נָמֵס|translate=it melts}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=15|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסֵ֫בָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נָסַבָּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=2}}; ''part''. {{GHGheb|text=נָמֵס|translate=molten}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָקֵל|translate=it is a light thing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=6}} (''perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=נָקַל}}); with ''ō'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָגֹ֫לּוּ|translate=they are rolled together}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=3|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=6}}b. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} with ''ō'' in the second syllable, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (from which König would also explain the ''perfects'' with ''ō''), we find {{GHGheb|text=תִּדֹּ֫מִּי|translate=thou shalt be brought to silence}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=2}} (unless this form should be referred to {{GHGterm|Qal}} with Qimḥi, Olshausen, König); {{GHGheb|text=יֵרוֹעַ|translate=he suffers hurt}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=20|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּרוֹץ}} (for ''tirrōṣ'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=29|verse=7}}; with ''ē'' in the second syllable {{GHGheb|text=תֵּחֵל|translate=she profanes herself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=9}}, but {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֵחַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=26}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יֵחָ֑ל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵחַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=8}}, &c. For ''infinitives'', cf. {{GHGheb|text=הִמֵּס|translate=to melt}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=3}} (as ''inf. constr.''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=10}} as ''inf. absol.''); again, with compensatory lengthening in the first syllable, {{GHGheb|text=הֵחֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, but with suffix {{GHGheb|text=הֵֽחַלּוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=4}}; also {{GHGheb|text=הִבּוֹז|translate=to be plundered}}, and {{GHGheb|text=הִבּוֹק|translate=to be emptied}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=3}}; in the {{GHGterm|imperative}}, only {{GHGheb|text=הִבָּ֫רוּ|translate=be ye clean}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=11}}. On {{GHGheb|text=הֵרֹ֫מּוּ|translate=get you up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=10}}, and the corresponding ''imperf.'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֹ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}}, &c., cf. {{GHGpar|72|dd}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|u}}
Examples of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} with sharpening of the initial syllable are, {{GHGheb|text=נִחַל|translate=it is profaned}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָלַל}}); {{GHGheb|text=נִחַר}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָרַר}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=4|hidebook=1}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נָחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=29}}); {{GHGheb|text=נִחַת|translate=fractus est}} (from {{GHGheb|text=חָתַת}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=5}}; cf. with this in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵֽחָמִים}} (for ''niḥḥāmîm'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=נֵֽאָרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=3|verse=9}}: in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive Niphʿal}} such a virtual strengthening of the guttural after preformatives never occurs.—The occurrence of ''u'' instead of ''ô'' as a separating vowel in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=נְשַׁדֻּ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mic|chapter=2|verse=4}} is abnormal.

{{center|III. ''On Hiphʿîl and Hophʿal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|v}}
6. The second syllable in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} sometimes has {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, especially under the influence of {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and the gutturals, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵמַר|translate=he made bitter}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵשַׁח|translate=he bowed}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵפַר|translate=he hath broken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=14}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}}, cf. {{GHGpar|29|q}}; otherwise {{GHGheb|text=הֵפֵר}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵפֵ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=5}}. In {{GHGheb|text=הֵפִיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=17|verse=19}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=34}}, and in {{GHGheb|text=הֵשׂ֫ירוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=4}} (perhaps also in {{GHGheb|text=יְחִיתַן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hab|chapter=2|verse=17}}, but cf. {{GHGpar|20|n}}) there is an assimilation to the corresponding forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, see z. Also {{GHGheb|text=הֵצַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=52}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵתַז}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}}; ''inf.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְהָבַֽר|translate=to cleanse}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=11}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}}. But also with other consonants, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵדַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=15}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵקַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵרַךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=16}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֵסַ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=9.10}} (and so usually in the 3rd ''plur. perf'', except before {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and gutturals, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵרֵ֫עוּ}}); ''imper.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁ֑ע|translate=besmear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָשַׁ֑מּוּ|translate=be astonished}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=5}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּרַ֫ע}} ''Thou dost afflict; part.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵצַל}} (on ''ē'' in the first syllable, see under i) ''shadowing'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=3}} (but {{GHGheb|text=מֵסִיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=24}} is assimilated to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, unless, with Moore, we simply read {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵךְ}}, or, with incorrect spelling, {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵיךְ}}. So in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲמִישֵׁ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=26}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, and in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲתִֽמְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|w}}
The ''ē'' of the second syllable, when without the tone, may become ''ĕ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫תֶל בִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=7}} (see also x). It is unusual (cf. {{GHGpar|53|k}}) to find the ''ē'' written fully as in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָפֵיר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=10}}. Instead of {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}} a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}<section end=par67 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
